\section[revistar]{revistar — to search (a person or a bag)}

\label{lesson:PT-C423-revistar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the padlock, then the Portuguese for to lose.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: revistar}
\textbf{revistar} — \textquotedblleft{}to search (a person or a bag)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
No aeroporto, revistaram a minha mochila.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{At the airport, they searched my backpack.}
\end{quote}

\emph{A revista} is the search, and also a magazine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{revistar} is built on \emph{revista} 'inspection, review', from \emph{rever} 'to look over again', which goes back to Latin \emph{vidēre} 'to see' (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{revistar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{revistar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{revistar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for the padlock, then the Portuguese for to lose, then say \emph{revistar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does revistar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To search (a person or a bag)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[declarar]{declarar — to declare}

\label{lesson:PT-C423-declarar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to lose, then the Portuguese for to search.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: declarar}
\textbf{declarar} — \textquotedblleft{}to declare\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Na alfândega, declaramos o que comprámos.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{At customs, we declare what we bought.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Nada a declarar} — nothing to declare.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{declarar} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{dēclārāre} 'to make clear' (EtymDB), built on \emph{clārus} 'clear'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{declarar}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{declarar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{declarar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to lose, then the Portuguese for to search, then say \emph{declarar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does declarar mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To declare\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[apreender]{apreender — to confiscate, to seize; to grasp (an idea)}

\label{lesson:PT-C423-apreender}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to search, then the Portuguese for to declare.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: apreender}
\textbf{apreender} — \textquotedblleft{}to confiscate, to seize; to grasp (an idea)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
A polícia apreendeu as garrafas de água.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The police confiscated the bottles of water.}
\end{quote}

Do not confuse with \emph{aprender}, to learn: same Latin root.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{apreender} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{apprehendere} 'to take hold of' (EtymDB), the same verb that gave the inherited \emph{aprender} 'to learn'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{apreender}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{apreender}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to search, then the Portuguese for to declare, then say \emph{apreender} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[o detetor]{o detetor — the detector}

\label{lesson:PT-C423-detetor}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to declare, then the Portuguese for to confiscate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o detetor}
\textbf{o detetor} — \textquotedblleft{}the detector\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O detetor fez barulho por causa do meu cinto.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The detector beeped because of my belt.}
\end{quote}

Spelled \emph{detetor} since the 1990 agreement; Brazil writes \emph{detector}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{detetor} is a learned formation on Latin \emph{dētegere, dētectum} 'to uncover', from \emph{tegere} 'to cover' (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o detetor}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o detetor}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{o detetor}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to declare, then the Portuguese for to confiscate, then say \emph{o detetor} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does o detetor mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The detector\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[carimbar]{carimbar — to stamp (a document)}

\label{lesson:PT-C423-carimbar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to confiscate, then the Portuguese for the detector.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: carimbar}
\textbf{carimbar} — \textquotedblleft{}to stamp (a document)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O polícia carimbou o meu passaporte.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The officer stamped my passport.}
\end{quote}

\emph{O carimbo} — the rubber stamp.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{carimbar} is built on \emph{carimbo} 'stamp', which EtymDB traces to Kimbundu, a language of Angola (\emph{ka'rima}).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{carimbar}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{carimbar}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for to confiscate, then the Portuguese for the detector, then say \emph{carimbar} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
